candidate.description: Join path from 200-people-worker PROCESS.md to the Unified Template v6.0.0 spine (US handoff invariant set, 24 layers). The subject is the medium itself — an executable process document being evaluated against the template that defines what an executable process IS. Three join routes evaluated: identity (PROC-200 → fleet → sovereign), structural (14 sections → 3 clusters → 24 layers), and data domain (slot_workbench.outreach_id → outreach spine).

join_path.spine: Unified Template v6.0.0 invariant set (US handoff, 24 layers L1-L24, 10 comparators)

identity_route.defect: heir.yaml declares hub_id=PROC-PEOPLE, PROCESS.md declares PROC-200. Two identifiers for one process. Join still resolves — both point to the same CTB position — but the conflict is a consistency fault in the routing key.

structural_route.defect: 20 of 24 layers have direct or transformed mappings from 03-map.json. 2 layers unresolved (L19 DMJ Define, L20 DMJ Map). 2 target layers unmapped by Define stage (L7 Resources, L10 DMJ parent). Structural join is incomplete but majority-attached — the gaps are in specific leaf layers, not in the trunk or cluster attachment.

data_domain_route.defect: None. OSAM §5 declares the join chain: slot_workbench → outreach_id. Single-table, self-contained. Direct join. No multi-hop resolution needed.

identity_conflicts_on_join_path.measurement: Count of identity values on the join path where multiple sources declare conflicting values for the same routing field. 0 = all identity fields consistent across all sources.
identity_conflicts_on_join_path.detail: Conflict 1: hub_id — heir.yaml says PROC-PEOPLE, PROCESS.md §1 says PROC-200. Conflict 2: governing_engine — heir.yaml references law/doctrine/TIER0_DOCTRINE.md which does not exist (renamed to FOUNDATIONAL_BEDROCK.md). Both are stale references, not structural breaks — the join resolves through CTB position regardless.

unresolved_structural_hops.measurement: Count of US handoff layers (L1-L24) where the map artifact classified the mapping as 'unresolved' — no source element exists to connect the subject to that layer. 0 = every layer on the spine has a source attachment.
unresolved_structural_hops.detail: L19 (DMJ Define table) — absent as formal 5-column schema. L20 (DMJ Map table) — absent as formal 3-column schema. Both are depth-3 leaves under L10. The subject performs equivalent functions (C&V in §6, OSAM in §5) but not in the target schema. The hop from subject to these layers does not resolve in the expected format.

unmapped_target_layers.measurement: Count of US handoff layers that the Define stage did not extract a source element for — the join cannot be tested because the mapping itself is absent. 0 = Define was exhaustive, all layers have something to join.
unmapped_target_layers.detail: L7 (Resources) — not extracted by Define stage. The subject likely has dependency/tool/secret information across ARCHITECTURE.md, DATA_SOURCE_REGISTRY.md, and heir.yaml but it was not defined as a discrete element. L10 (DMJ parent container) — children are unresolved so parent container has no structural content to evaluate.

join_hop_count.measurement: Number of intermediate hops required to reach the spine from the subject's identity. 0 = direct attachment (subject IS the spine instance). Lower = simpler join, less ambiguity.
join_hop_count.detail: The subject IS the medium being evaluated. PROCESS.md is an instance of 'executable process' — the exact medium the Unified Template defines. The join is direct: no intermediate lookup, no fuzzy matching, no multi-hop resolution. The document attaches to the template at L1 (root) and every layer below is a structural check against that direct attachment.

stale_reference_count.measurement: Count of references on the join path that point to renamed, moved, or non-existent targets. 0 = all references resolve to current targets.
stale_reference_count.detail: Stale 1: heir.yaml governing_engine → law/doctrine/TIER0_DOCTRINE.md (file renamed to FOUNDATIONAL_BEDROCK.md). Stale 2: standalone OSAM.md references old table names (people_company_slot, people_people_master) while PROCESS.md §5 references slot_workbench. Neither breaks the join — the primary document (PROCESS.md) has correct references — but the secondary files carry dead pointers.
